title: Adaptive eval cadence and rollback matrix for fractional rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define an operationally lightweight but statistically robust cadence and decision matrix for fractional rollouts (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) used across console and hosted APIs. Goal is to reduce time-to-rollout for low-risk changes while preventing quality regressions for high-impact features.

Scope: Applies to feature flags, model variants (model family or quantization change), routing policy adjustments, and non-invasive UI changes that affect inference traffic. Does NOT cover schema-breaking API changes or infra upgrades (those follow separate upgrade playbooks).

What this ticket delivers: a documented milestone cadence, exact metric contracts (primary/secondary), acceptance thresholds for each ramp, instrumentation requirements, escalation ladder, a rollback matrix with metric-based triggers, and a short runbook snippet to embed in canary jobs.

Trade-offs considered: We biased toward shorter evaluation windows for low-traffic customers (to reduce time-to-revenue) while requiring stricter statistical smoothing for model-quality metrics (to avoid false positives from noisy eval signals). The matrix uses both absolute thresholds and relative deltas to protect against noisy baselines.

Artifacts and links:
- PRD (high-level background): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Adaptive+Eval+Cadence+PRD
- Draft dashboard & alert pack: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/experiments/adaptive-eval-pack
- Proposed gating library prototype (infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-gates/pull/42
acceptance_criteria: A concise milestone table exists mapping traffic percent -> min duration -> primary metric thresholds
Dashboards show live canary cohorts and historical baselines for all primary metrics
Automated canary job (1%, 5%, 25%) can run with the gating library and emit decisions (pass/warn/fail)
Runbook contains explicit escalation steps and a tested rollback command for both hosted and dedicated environments
Stakeholders (Eng, SRE, Design) have reviewed and signed off on thresholds in the doc
milestones: M0 - Preflight (docs + infra): define metrics, add instrumentation hooks, provision canary cohorts. Target complete by 2025-02-21

M1 - Alpha (1%): run 72-hour active evaluation window; require no P95 latency regression > +25ms and error rate delta <= +0.1%. If model-quality metric (eval-set delta) degrades > 0.6%, fail and rollback immediately.
M2 - Beta (5%): run 48-hour evaluation with additional user metric checks (CTR/engagement proxies). Allow small transient latency bumps but require long-tail error stability.
M3 - Ramp (25%): run 24-48 hour check focused on cost and sustained quality. If cost per token increases > 12% with no quality improvement, trigger manual review before continuing.
M4 - Full (100%): final verification for 7 days of steady-state monitoring; schedule postmortem if any secondary metric regresses beyond caution thresholds
instrumentation: Token-level breakdown: per-route p50/p95/p99 with rolling 10-minute window
Model-quality eval: batched eval set run every 12 hours with delta and 95% CI
User-signal proxies: sampled request-level event correlation (1 in 1000) to link feature changes to downstream metrics
Automated gating output: standardized JSON decision object pushed to events bus and recorded to experiment table
